title: THE BLOOD WAS NOT BROUGHT IN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Since its blood was not taken into the Holy Place, you should have eaten the goat in the sanctuary area, as I commanded.'" - Lev 10:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses' reasoning is precise. The rule was clear: sin offerings whose blood went into the Holy Place were burned entirely; those whose blood stayed outside were eaten by the priests. This goat's blood had not gone in. Therefore it should have been eaten.

Moses knew the law thoroughly and applied it exactly.

That is not a small thing. In a moment of crisis and grief, he was still reasoning carefully from what God had actually said, rather than from feeling or assumption.

We could learn from that. Much confusion in the Christian life comes from imprecise handling of Scripture — half-remembered verses, principles applied where they do not belong, promises claimed out of context.

Paul told Timothy to be a worker who does not need to be ashamed and who correctly handles the word of truth (2 Tim 2:15). The Bereans examined the Scriptures every day to see if what Paul said was true (Acts 17:11) — and Luke calls them noble for it.

Knowing your Bible well is not academic fussiness. It is how you avoid being blown around by whatever sounds spiritual this year.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I know Scripture well enough to reason carefully from it?
2. Have I accepted spiritual claims without checking them against the Bible?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me a careful love for Your Word. Help me to handle it accurately and to be shaped by what it actually says. Amen.
